**Title:**
Why Temporal Abstraction Can Fail in Imagination-Based RL: A Diagnostic Analysis of Variable-Rate DreamerV3

**Abstract:**
World-model reinforcement learning increasingly targets continuous control tasks where temporal abstraction enables planning across heterogeneous time scales. We find that Δt-conditioning, effective in model-predictive control (MPC), cannot transfer to imagination-based actor-critic training: every variable-rate DreamerV3 configuration suffers substantial performance degradation. Factorial diagnostics on two continuous-control tasks identify the combination of trained temporal embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the strongest predictor of this failure, conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO; AUROC=1.000, n=36). The recurrent state-space model (RSSM) develops a reward prediction gap at Δt>1 that the critic internalizes as optimistic values; the contrast with MPC identifies feedback architecture as a hypothesized structural factor. Gradient, output, and representation interventions fail to eliminate CIVO; at the architecture level, dual critics converge in pure imagination, but wide dual-critic (min-aggregation + increased capacity) achieves partial prevention, the only positive result, highlighting open challenges in the architectural design of variable-rate model-based RL.

**Primary Keyword:**
Video models and latent world models for robot learning

（论文核心是 DreamerV3 的 RSSM latent world model 中 temporal conditioning 的失败模式，最匹配这个 keyword。次选是 "Model-based and model-free learning for robotic control"。）
